newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: SAfrica gets second commercial-scale gold refinery.
newsitem.headline: SAfrica gets second commercial-scale gold refinery.

text.p: Randgold and Exploration Co Ltd said on Thursday that the board of its Harmony Gold Mining Co Ltd had given the go-ahead for the establishment of a commercial-scale gold refinery, only the second in South Africa.
Work on the refinery will start immediately and is scheduled for completion in the third quarter of 1997.
The refinery has been designed to produce two tonnes of 99.99 percent pure gold per month -- sufficient to process Harmony's total gold output.

The cost of establishing the plant and acquiring technology from Mintek will be 3.3 million rand, which is less than the annual savings Harmony expects to achieve by smelting and refining its own gold.
Harmony has applied to the Treasury for permission to market its own gold internationally. To date there has been no response to this request.
At present, all South African gold is refined at the Rand Refinery, owned collectively by the mining industry -- and the central Reserve Bank is the sole marketer of South African gold.

Harmony managing director Bernard Swanepoel said the decision to establish a refinery was another step in the process of transforming Harmony from a gold producer with a limited life into a broadly-based gold mining and exploration business with long-term prospects.
